In healthy individuals, the concurrent administration of daptomycin (CUBICIN) and simvastatin does not affect the plasma trough concentrations of simvastatin, and no cases of skeletal myopathy have been reported. However, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, such as statins, are known to potentially cause myopathy, which is characterized by muscle pain or weakness accompanied by elevated creatine phosphokinase (CPK) levels. 2. In a Phase 3 clinical trial for Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia/endocarditis, some patients who had received prior or concurrent treatment with an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor developed elevated CPK levels. Since clinical experience with the coadministration of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and daptomycin is limited, it is advisable to consider temporarily discontinuing the use of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors in patients receiving daptomycin. 3. Daptomycin at clinically relevant plasma concentrations has been observed to cause a significant, concentration-dependent false prolongation of prothrombin time (PT) and elevation of the International Normalized Ratio (INR) when certain recombinant thromboplastin reagents are used in the assay. To minimize the risk of falsely elevated PT/INR results due to this interaction, it is recommended to collect specimens for PT/INR testing near the time of daptomycin trough plasma concentrations. However, even at trough levels, sufficient daptomycin concentrations may still cause this interaction. 4. If PT/INR values obtained at trough remain substantially elevated beyond expected levels, alternative methods for PT/INR evaluation should be considered. Additionally, other potential causes of abnormally elevated PT/INR results should be investigated. 5. Long-term carcinogenicity studies in animals have not been conducted to assess the carcinogenic potential of daptomycin. However, a battery of genotoxicity tests, including the Ames assay, mammalian cell gene mutation assay, chromosomal aberration test in Chinese hamster ovary cells, in vivo micronucleus assay, in vitro DNA repair assay, and in vivo sister chromatid exchange assay in Chinese hamsters, revealed no evidence of mutagenic or clastogenic potential. 6. Daptomycin did not impair fertility or reproductive performance in male and female rats when administered intravenously at doses up to 150 mg/kg/day, which is approximately nine times the estimated human exposure level based on area under the curve (AUC). 7. Daptomycin is classified as Pregnancy Category B. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of daptomycin in pregnant women. Embryofetal development studies in rats and rabbits at doses up to 75 mg/kg (equivalent to 2 and 4 times the human dose of 6 mg/kg, respectively, based on body surface area) showed no evidence of harm to the fetus. However, because animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response, daptomycin should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. 8. Daptomycin is present in human breast milk but has poor oral bioavailability. Caution should be exercised when administering daptomycin to nursing women. 9. The safety and effectiveness of daptomycin in pediatric patients under the age of 18 years have not been established. 10. In Phase 3 clinical trials of complicated skin and skin structure infections (cSSSI), 27% of patients treated with daptomycin were aged 65 years or older, and 12% were aged 75 years or older. In the Phase 3 trial for Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia/endocarditis, 25% of patients were aged 65 years or older, and 16% were aged 75 years or older. Clinical success rates were lower in patients aged 65 years or older compared to those under 65 years of age. Additionally, treatment-emergent adverse events were more common in patients aged 65 years or older. Although daptomycin exposure was higher in healthy elderly subjects compared to younger subjects, no dosage adjustment is necessary for elderly patients with creatinine clearance (CLCR) ≥ 30 mL/min. 11. Daptomycin is primarily eliminated by the kidneys. Therefore, a modification of the dosing interval is recommended for patients with creatinine clearance (CLCR) < 30 mL/min, including those undergoing hemodialysis or continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD).
